$comment: Per-project overlay for code-design-audit. Copy to <repo>/eval/audit/config.json and fill. RULE: the checks are project-agnostic; everything project-specific lives HERE. Never hardcode a scale, a path or a product term inside a check. Every ledger entry (outOfScope / exceptions / nodeExceptions) carries a `reason` — it is debt on the record, not a setting. Do NOT fabricate any of these values: if the human hasn't stated them, ask (propose-first).

tokenSources.$comment: Where the scale actually lives. Spacing/radius/type/colour scales are DERIVED from these at runtime, so a token added here needs no check edit.

roots.$comment: Source roots the walker scans. `screens` is the router root used to resolve a registry route to a file.

ignore: <glob or path fragment to skip entirely>
typeScale$comment: Font sizes (px) transcribed from the design file's text styles. Empty = the type lens cannot run; say so rather than inventing a scale.

scaleExtras.$comment: Values legitimately on-scale but not derivable from a token declaration. Each key that gets a value also gets a `<key>$comment` stating WHY.

copy.$comment: Pure product vocabulary. Guessing this produces noise on every acronym in the product.

owners.$comment: Check id → the ARTEFACT the fix belongs in. Attached to each finding so routing survives a session that never reads the skill. `code` = the design file cannot express it. `figma` = a design/token decision the code only mirrors (a code-only fix creates drift the pixel gate will then report as a regression). `both` = the same edit lands twice (copy). `verify` = undecidable statically; the geometry measurement resolves it. `process` = neither artefact — the harness itself.

collapse.$comment: Checks folded to one row per file — real but systemic, so the per-file count is the actionable unit.

outOfScope.$comment: Files this gate REPORTS on but must not FAIL on, because nothing here can verify a fix (e.g. a layer with no captured baseline). Capped at WARN and labelled, never hidden. Removing a name from this list is what 'capturing a baseline' means — the list is the ledger of what is still unmeasured, and it shrinks.
outOfScope.label: <why these are unverifiable, in one phrase>

exceptions$comment: Accepted findings. Shape: { check, file, reason }. `reason` must state what was MEASURED, not that it looked fine.
nodeExceptions$comment: Accepted per-node geometry findings. Shape: { check, path, prop, reason }. A false acquittal here whitewashes real drift — narrow each entry to the specific property and keep the measurement in the reason.
